significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that "a small set of attention heads" preserves an agent-specific stale state while distinct world-tracking heads preserve the current state, with selective ablations producing opposite belief/world errors; this is a form-(ii) causal decomposition, not merely an existence claim, and it establishes both a false-belief phenomenon and a mechanism. It would fix explanations of why models default to reality in Sally–Anne-style tasks and distinguish failures of agent-state maintenance from failures of world-state tracking, a distinction behaviorally exercised by ToMi (Le et al., 2019) and FANToM (Kim et al., 2023). Verified false would rule out the definite localized dual-circuit account—though not distributed or model-dependent belief mechanisms—so the branches are distinguishable and moderately informative. Topic substitution does not preserve this score: generic research on LLM beliefs would not supply the claim-specific, independently manipulable belief-versus-world decomposition that supports a score above the topic median.

reach.justification: The concrete handles are the "candidate 'false-belief heads'" and their ablation or patching as interventions, but these are principally post-hoc tools for attributing an already observed false-belief error rather than ex-ante predictors with an action window. After re-extraction on another model, the conclusion does not predict a scaling law, threshold, ordering, or other numerical relation; it mainly supplies a procedure for locating potentially different circuitry. Although the record mentions tests of "non-spatial belief items" and "second-order false belief," it does not affirm that transfer as part of the hypothesis, so the warranted downstream scope is mainly mechanistic-interpretability researchers studying first-order false belief rather than general auditors or deployment practitioners. Topic substitution would remove the named heads and interventions and leave no reusable handle, so the topic alone would score below 5; the claim-specific handle raises reach only to the topic-median range.
